classification.difficultyReason: Rearrange each product equation and combine horizontal and vertical translations, asymptotes and exact intercepts.

answer.short:
$y=3+\dfrac{2}{x-4}$. Asymptotes: $x=4$ and $y=3$. Intercepts: $\left(\dfrac{10}{3},0\right)$ and $\left(0,\dfrac52\right)$.

Translate $y=\dfrac2x$ four units right and three units up.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y-3&=\frac{2}{x-4}\\y&=3+\frac{2}{x-4}\end{align*}$$
Translate $y=\dfrac2x$ four units right and three units up. The asymptotes are $x=4$ and $y=3$.

For the $x$-intercept, set $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}3+\frac{2}{x-4}&=0\\\frac{2}{x-4}&=-3\\x-4&=-\frac23\\x&=\frac{10}{3}\end{align*}$$
For the $y$-intercept, set $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=3+\frac{2}{0-4}\\y&=\frac52\end{align*}$$
Draw the branches above-right and below-left of the asymptote intersection $(4,3)$, approaching both asymptotes.

answer.short:
$y=3+\dfrac{2}{x-2}$. Asymptotes: $x=2$ and $y=3$. Intercepts: $\left(\dfrac43,0\right)$ and $(0,2)$.

Translate $y=\dfrac2x$ two units right and three units up.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}y-3&=\frac{2}{x-2}\\y&=3+\frac{2}{x-2}\end{align*}$$
Translate $y=\dfrac2x$ two units right and three units up. The asymptotes are $x=2$ and $y=3$.

For the $x$-intercept, set $y=0$:
$$\begin{align*}3+\frac{2}{x-2}&=0\\\frac{2}{x-2}&=-3\\x-2&=-\frac23\\x&=\frac43\end{align*}$$
For the $y$-intercept, set $x=0$:
$$\begin{align*}y&=3+\frac{2}{0-2}\\y&=2\end{align*}$$
Draw the branches above-right and below-left of the asymptote intersection $(2,3)$, approaching both asymptotes.
